text:
dana: Noticed a cluster blip in ap-southeast1 around 06:10 UTC. GPU attaches started timing out and a handful of nodes reported metadata checksum errors on local NVMe during scrub waves.
sam: any host ids / logs?
dana: sample dmesg from gnode-apse1-078:
```
[  370.123456] scrubber: metadata checksum mismatch on inode 3456789, correcting
[  370.123789] nvme nvme0n1: timeout waiting for completion
[  370.124000] provisioner: attach: scratch allocation timed out
```
dana: iostat snapshot during the window showed avgqu-sz spiking and %util ~96:
```
Device:       r/s    w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  avgqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1      0.2  900.0   0.5  36000.0    10.5    96.1
```
maria: did we change scrub settings recently?
nori: yes, yesterday we pushed a change to accelerate metadata scrubs across hosts (scrub_concurrency 2 -> 8) to reduce long-term drift. that increased parallel small writes and caused thermal fanspin in some host batches.
sam: blast radius?
dana: roughly 18% of gpu attach attempts in that AZ failed for ~6 minutes. most retried and recovered but job start latencies spiked and a few orchestrator retries hit backoff. no customer-facing outages yet.
maria: cost/latency tradeoff: slowing scrubs delays detection of real corruption but avoids attach disruption. prefer targeted rollback if it's the culprit.
nori: short term mitigation: 1) revert scrub_concurrency to 2 on a 6-host canary 2) add a lightweight metadata-only scrub mode that avoids heavy rewrite batches 3) add host-level nvme util guard to pause scrub when util > 85% 4) route new GPU allocs from the affected pool to eu-west as a fallback.
dana: rolling canary now. ops-bot create incident please.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2104 created: "ap-southeast1 nvme metadata-scrub burst -> gpu attach timeouts" (severity: medium)
sam: paste rollout plan and dashboards pls. hold for 15m after canary.
nori: plan: revert concurrency on canary hosts, monitor attach_success_rate, nvme %util, scrub error counts. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv?n=scrub-ops
maria: note: routing to eu-west adds ~20% cost for those batch jobs; prefer config rollback if effective.
dana: canary shows attach success back to normal after ~90s. expanding rollout. will follow up with a postmortem if everything stays green. :thumbsup:
